scope: Independent fresh Acorn hosted test installation; no production

Healthy staged verification without activation; explicit activation retained fence 0
Live resource inspection proved one physical D1 and all seven D1 binding aliases targeting it
Selected two-product paid checkout settled; one invitation delivered and both products offered
Browser submission, stale moderation revision rejected with 409, exact revision published
Published product summary showed one 5-star review; the other product remained empty
Declined checkout produced no invitation; unsubscribe suppressed a later selected purchase
Checkout settled while Reviews returned 503; restore resumed normal checkpoint processing
Missing producer D1 binding and version drift diagnosed; recorded producer version restored
Same-source upgrade, controlled interrupted deployment and documented upgrade resume
Healthy pause, explicit reactivation replay and final healthy pause; unsubscribe still available
limitations: Timings are observations, not an isolated causal benchmark; network, cache and warm-state differences apply.
Final frozen-head upgrade/rollback used the same source commit, not a second compatible application revision.
Commerce-only topology was tested locally but was not hosted in this run.
Node 24.21.0 was used; the guide requires Node 24 and .nvmrc pins 24.20.0.
Four pre-existing high npm tooling advisories remain; locked dependencies were unchanged.
Fault injection used an external qualification harness, not a documented merchant command.
No pre-activation purchase was made; staged state and absence of an activation record were verified.
privacy: Resource identifiers, provider identities, mailboxes, capabilities, keys and private paths omitted. Detailed evidence remains private.
